title: UK ETS biomass zero-rating and sustainability QA controls

sources.title: UK ETS technical guidance: Monitoring and Reporting Regulation (MRR) 2018
UK Emissions Trading Scheme: monitoring and reporting biomass in installations

facts.source_fact: Operators using solid or gaseous biomass can apply an emission factor of zero to the biomass fraction under the linked UK ETS biomass guidance.
facts.expected_handling: Apply zero rating only to the qualifying biomass fraction.

facts.source_fact: Bioliquids used for non-energy purposes can apply zero factor to the biomass fraction under the guidance.
GHGE permit holders using bioliquids to generate energy must retain verifier evidence that applicable sustainability criteria are met to use zero rating.
facts.expected_handling: Require sustainability evidence before zero rating energy bioliquids.

facts.source_fact: HSE permit holders using bioliquids may apply zero factor to the biomass fraction without demonstrating the same sustainability criteria.
facts.expected_handling: Apply the HSE-specific modification only to HSE permits.

facts.source_fact: Bioliquid sustainability compliance is relevant to monitoring and reporting emissions, not to whether an installation is in UK ETS scope.
facts.expected_handling: Do not use sustainability failure as an installation-scope test.

facts.source_fact: Operators must report a preliminary emission factor for biomass used, including where biomass fraction is greater than 97 percent.
facts.expected_handling: Retain preliminary factors even when reportable emissions are zero-rated.

facts.source_fact: The guidance identifies land-use and lifecycle greenhouse-gas-emission-savings sustainability criteria for bioliquids.
Recognised voluntary-scheme certificates may support verifier evidence, but operators must check recognition scope and supply-chain coverage.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat any certificate as universally sufficient.

facts.source_fact: Evidence of voluntary-scheme compliance is required for each fuel consignment.
Where no recognised scheme is used, the guidance allows default, actual, or combined greenhouse-gas-emissions values subject to the applicable methodology and retained evidence.
facts.expected_handling: Record method and evidence for the selected value basis.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve linked UK ETS biomass guidance facts.
Apply zero factor only to qualifying biomass fraction.
Separate GHGE and HSE permit rules.
Distinguish energy and non-energy bioliquid use.
Check applicable land-use and GHG-saving evidence.
Keep preliminary factors in monitoring records.
Keep certificate evidence per consignment and supply chain.
Use the version linked by the current MRR collection and defer to legislation on conflict.
Flag permit, sustainability, fraction or evidence conflicts.
